Matt Henry to Gurnoor Brar, no run, fullish outside off, Gurnoor Brar gets forward to push, no feet and he is beaten
Matt Henry to Gurnoor Brar, no run, wide of the crease and short of length outside off, Gurnoor Brar again is beaten as he plays a leaden-footed poke

Matt Henry to Gurnoor Brar, no run, Matt Henry has pinged Gurnoor Brar on the right arm! This is a short delivery and targetting Brar who looks to fend at that, the ball misses the glove and pings him on the right arm. He doesn't call for the physio and is ready to face the next ball
Matt Henry to Gurnoor Brar, THATS OUT!! Bowled!!

No feet from Brar as Matt Henry bowls the very full delivery on off, the seam came out scrambled and Brar stays leg-side of the ball, pushes at it and it sneaks under the bat to hit the base of off-stump. New Zealand have thumped India by 244 runs as the series heads to the decider on the same ground 2-1 in favor of India. Gurnoor Brar b Matt Henry 2(13)
India would be happy that Matt Henry won't be there for Sunday's decider as the pacer will join the ones who are preparing for the Tests against India coming up.

Matt Henry | Player of the Match (1/2): Great to be back. Obviously it's been a funny odd year. So, good to be back here with some one-day cricket. [On his recovery and missing the previous matches] It wasn't ideal, colliding heads with Dev (Devon Conway). I think I take a bit of responsibility on that one too. So, not ideal, but it just pushed things back a little bit. But thankfully we're doing alright now. [On the workload management] Yeah, I think that was the key part. Obviously once you have a head knock like that, you just got to be really careful and it pushed things back a bit. But this is really key for moving forward to what is a huge summer for us. [On his 1st over - triple wicket maiden] Yeah, it's quite funny, isn't it? The wind was so strong and it was keeping things pretty simple, and it's funny when you're actually trying to have a simple game plan. A bit of luck as well. One shot a little bit low there too, so maybe the wind pushed me a bit sideways (smiles).

Henry (2/2): [Bowling strategy] Well, especially with the way the wind was going, I wasn't too worried about the swing. So from ball one it was just about trying to have the strengths and bring the stumps in play, really. We knew that there was a small window there with the new ball that you could put the batters under pressure. So just trying to be as simple as possible, obviously, and when it moves sharply like that in the first over, when people are facing first ball, it's pretty tough. [On his successes against India] Oh, I don't want to get too carried away. No, they're a world-class outfit, and I think that's the message that we were saying right through. They can bat deep, and yeah, look, it's one game and we've got another one coming up soon that hopefully we can level the series. [On the transition to Test cricket] Yeah, join in with the Test squad. We've got a bit of a training camp, just get the red ball in hand and then just get ready for next week.

The conditions were much better today, possibly the best for batting in this series. Yet, it turned out to be a one-sided encounter. The game was won or lost in the first powerplay. NZ scored 72/0, India dropped Young twice in the 2nd over and he went on to score a century. In the second essay, Matt Henry more or less sealed the game in the very first over by dismissing Rohit, Kohli and Shreyas Iyer for ducks. Henry won't be available for the final ODI, but he has got some much-needed game time ahead of the Tests. That's it for today. We'll be back on Sunday (November 15th) for the fifth and final ODI which will be played at the same venue. Until next time, it's goodbye...
